subject.title: Model safety/alignment can block explicitly authorized operational tasks (e.g. SSH diagnostics)

question: Should OpenClaw define a trusted-operator diagnostics contract for authorized read-only infrastructure work, or keep model/provider refusals terminal except for narrower provider-approved fallback paths?
rationale: The remaining work changes how model safety decisions interact with operator authority and infrastructure tooling, so automation should not choose the safety boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Define Narrow Trusted Diagnostics
options.body: Add explicit refusal/auth/tool-failure observability and read-only execution guidance for authorized operator diagnostics while preserving destructive-action approvals and provider/tool policy boundaries.

options.title: Improve Diagnostics Only
options.body: Make model refusal, authorization denial, and SSH/tool failure visibly distinct without changing the model's bias toward executing infrastructure requests.

options.title: Limit To Provider Fallbacks
options.body: Let the narrower provider-refusal issue and PRs decide fallback behavior and leave the broader SSH/operator-authority contract out of scope for now.

recommendation.title: Define Narrow Trusted Diagnostics
recommendation.body: Add explicit refusal/auth/tool-failure observability and read-only execution guidance for authorized operator diagnostics while preserving destructive-action approvals and provider/tool policy boundaries.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the most recent merged refusal/fallback subset and is the strongest available routing candidate for the product/security boundary.
